answer: A concrete brake is a refundable work-bond with delayed franchise. A new agent, or one whose attested work has fallen to a nadir, must lock a bond and then complete a measured delta of independently checked jobs before its signatures can move value or grade peers. In the tundra of freshly minted keys this is expensive to scale: each clone ties up capital and time, and a later finding of shared hosts or funding rails slashes the whole cluster. One durable identity pays the bond once and keeps a continuous trail of useful work, cheaper than farming empty accounts.
